params.body:
Ilse asked for this in the same breath as the Vanhees report: *"Het zou misschien ook gemakkelijk zijn om hiervan een melding te krijgen via het grijze belletje als dat kan?"*

It is well aimed. On 26 September a purchase lost both its confirmation mails and neither garage knew anything about it. A bell notification is a second channel that does not hang off the mail server, which is exactly what was missing.

Both garages now get one after a buy-over, each in the language of the **receiving** garage.

## Its own notification class, not the generic one

`GenericNotification` is deliberately one shape for everything, database only, with the caller composing the sentences — its own docblock says "geen mail/broadcast in deze eerste versie". For a message that has two sides, four languages, and that ought to carry the mail too, that is the wrong direction: it pushes text and localisation onto whoever calls it.

`VehicleChangedHands` knows its own text, localises itself through `->locale()`, and has a `via()` where a channel can be added.

`Notify::dealerWith()` sits beside `Notify::dealer()` so one place still knows that notifying a garage means notifying all of its users; what is in the message, and later which channels carry it, belongs to the notification.

**The follow-up this sets up, deliberately not today:** add `mail` to `via()` and fold `SoldEmail` and `SoldBuyerEmail` into it. Then there is one message with two channels instead of two hand-written paths — which is precisely what failed on the 26th, when the mails hung off a branch that was never reached. That is a rebuild of a working mail path and deserves its own change.

## Two things this PR got wrong first

**The rule number.** I read the highest `R S5-3.x` off a sort that spanned sections and picked `.11`, which already exists. `RulesIdentityTest` caught the duplicate. It is `R S5-3.15`.

**The language test.** It called `toArray()` directly and asserted that Dutch and French differed. They did not, and the code was right: `->locale()` is applied by Laravel's *sender*, which sets the locale around rendering and restores it afterwards. A direct call skips that and can never show what a recipient reads. The test now sends for real and reads the row back out of `notifications`, which is the only version of this worth trusting.

## Verified

Four tests: each side gets its own message with the car and the other garage in it, each garage reads it in its own language with no translation key leaking through, all four languages carry all four texts, and the bell hangs in its own `try` beside the mails so a broken bell cannot take a mail with it.

New rule R S5-3.15. `phpstan` green, `pint` green. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment.
params.title: The bell says a car changed hands
